title: Recovering the false-restriction from average and half-difference
statement:
Let $f$ be a Boolean function on $n+1$ variables, and let $x$ be a point of the $n$-dimensional Boolean hypercube. Then the restriction of $f$ obtained by fixing its last coordinate to $\mathrm{false}$ equals the sum of the average and the half-difference of $f$ over that coordinate:
\[
f(x,\mathrm{false}) = \frac{f(x,\mathrm{false}) + f(x,\mathrm{true})}{2} + \frac{f(x,\mathrm{false}) - f(x,\mathrm{true})}{2}.
\]
hypotheses_covered: f is a Boolean function on n+1 variables
x is a point of the n-dimensional Boolean hypercube
replaced:
For every $x$, the restriction of $f$ fixing the last coordinate to false equals the sum of
the average and the half-difference: $\mathrm{restrictLast}\,f\,\mathrm{false}\,x = \mathrm{avgLast}\,f\,x + \mathrm{diffLast}\,f\,x$.
